title: Ischia + the Bay of Naples — June 2027

packing: Water shoes for everyone: Sorgeto’s hot-spring cove and several coves are pebble-and-rock entries.
Reef-safe sunscreen and swim shirts: the schedule averages four-plus water hours a day at 79°F.
One packable tote per person: beach-and-bus days work out of totes, not the big bags, which never leave Forio.
Motion-sickness tabs: one hydrofoil each way plus two ferry days — cheap insurance for the 8-year-old.
Passports + ETIAS printouts: Italy is Schengen; check ETIAS status before travel.

itinerary.labelHtml:
Day by Day

Seven nights, one base, no car

Forio holds every night. Boats and buses carry the days, and Saturday absorbs whatever the wind postpones.

days.heading: Pittsburgh → Newark → overnight to Naples
days.feel: One connection, then sleep over the Atlantic

facts.label: Flight
facts.valueHtml: PIT → EWR → NAP · United, single ticket

days.note: United’s Naples nonstop leaves Newark in the late afternoon or evening, so a midday PIT → EWR hop connects with slack. Mid-June is United’s one-flight-a-day window on this route — a misconnect means 24 hours, not three days, but build the buffer anyway.

days.heading: Naples → hydrofoil → Forio
days.feel: Land, cross the bay, unpack once

facts.label: Transfer
facts.valueHtml: Alibus ~$6pp → Molo Beverello → Alilauro hydrofoil ~50 min

days.note: The Alibus runs every 15–30 minutes from the terminal to the port, and Alilauro serves Forio direct — no Naples logistics beyond one bus. If the sea is up, the slow car ferry from Porta di Massa almost never cancels; take it and lose an hour, not the day.

days.heading: Forio + Chiaia beach
days.feel: A deliberately soft first full day

facts.label: Water
facts.valueHtml: Sea about 74°F — warm enough to stay in

days.note: Walk Forio, claim a stretch of Chiaia or San Francesco beach, and let the jet lag drain. The Soccorso church two blocks from town is the sunset ritual all week. Nothing today is allowed to have a ticket.

days.heading: Giardini Poseidon thermal day

facts.label: Rule
facts.valueHtml: Under-12s: seawater pools + beach, not thermal pools

days.note: Twenty-two pools terraced above Citara Bay, graded from 61°F to 104°F. Split coverage: one parent rotates the hot pools with the 13-year-old, the other holds the seawater pools and beach with the 8-year-old, swap after lunch.

spots.name: Poseidon Gardens + Citara Bay
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · poseidonIG · citaraFlickr

spots.cost: Giardini Poseidon’s published 2026 tariff is about $55 adult full day, $50 from 1 p.m., ages 4–11 half price — about $190 for this family. The one rule that shapes the day: under-12s are not allowed in the thermal pools, only the three seawater pools and the beach. The 13-year-old gets all 22 pools; the 8-year-old still gets a full beach-and-pool day.
spots.climate: Sea about 74°F by mid-June and the island’s driest stretch of the year. Poseidon’s pools are graded 61–104°F, so a cool morning or a windy afternoon never cancels the day.
spots.saveHtml: Save The afternoon ticket (from 1 p.m.) saves about $22 for the family and still leaves four hours of pools; Citara’s public beach next door is free all week.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge One full-day Poseidon visit is the trip’s signature purchase. Negombo on San Montano bay is the second thermal park if the family wants a rematch — note its child pricing runs by height, and both kids likely pay as adults there.
spots.restoHtml:
• La Tinaia — family trattoria in Forio center; plain pasta on request and a famous lemon spaghetti
  • Pizzeria Di Meglio — frequently called the island’s best pizza, near San Francesco beach
  • La Ruota — beachfront on Chiaia — swim, then eat without moving the towels
spots.altboxHtml:
• Negombo (San Montano) if Poseidon reads as too big — smaller, greener, on the island’s calmest swimming bay.
  • San Montano bay on its own — shallow, warm and the best pure kid-swim on Ischia, no park ticket required.

days.heading: Castello Aragonese + Ischia Ponte
days.feel: The island’s icon, then its beach
days.note: Bus across the island, walk the causeway, take the elevator up and the ramparts slowly. The beach beside the causeway fills the afternoon, and a floodlit-castle dinner in Ischia Ponte is the night to stay out late.

spots.name: Castello Aragonese + Ischia Ponte
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · castelloIG · ischiaponteFlickr

spots.cost: Castello Aragonese is about $13 adult, $7 ages 10–18, free under 10 — about $40 for this family, elevator included, and the ticket allows same-day re-entry. The stone causeway, the ramparts and the olive-terrace views are most of the visit; budget a gelato-paced half day.
spots.climate: June averages 79°F with about seven brief rain days for the whole month. The castle is an open-air site with real sun exposure — do it before lunch and leave the afternoon for the beach below.
spots.saveHtml: Save The castle’s ~$40 family total is the cheapest headline attraction on this board; the beach on either side of the causeway is free.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Dinner in Ischia Ponte with the castle floodlit — the malcbawn boat-and-castle shot in this carousel is a normal Tuesday here.
spots.restoHtml:
• Il Terrazzo (in the castle) — café-terrace inside the walls for mid-visit bribes
  • Ischia Ponte trattorias — plain pasta and pizza line the causeway street
  • CS/CD bus back to Forio — runs until late; no driving, no parking
spots.altboxHtml:
• Sant’Angelo — the car-free pastel village on the south coast, saved here for Saturday.
  • Mount Epomeo’s summit walk from Fontana (about 2–2.5 hours round trip) if the family wants one real hike with a 360° bay view.

days.heading: Procida day trip
days.note: The Bay’s most photogenic harbor is one short crossing from Casamicciola. Climb to Terra Murata for the postcard angle, eat on the Corricella front, and be back on Ischia for an evening swim.

spots.name: Procida day trip
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · procidaIG · corricellaFlickr

images.alt: Procida’s Marina Corricella pastel houses glowing at dusk above the fishing fleet
Aerial view of Procida’s colored waterfront and boat harbor
Bird’s-eye panorama of Corricella’s amphitheater of houses meeting the water

Naples harbor from the air with Vesuvius rising behind the city
Panoramic view over Naples rooftops toward a hazy Vesuvius

Castel dell’Ovo on the Naples waterfront in bright summer light
Pompeii’s forum columns under a dramatic golden sky
A ferry crossing the Bay of Naples at dusk below the silhouette of Vesuvius

spots.cost: Ischia → Procida ferries run 15–30 minutes, up to a dozen sailings a day, roughly $14–21 per person round trip from Casamicciola — call it $65–90 for four. Marina Corricella and the Terra Murata viewpoint are free; lunch on the harbor is the day’s real spend.
spots.climate: Same forgiving June as Ischia — around 79°F and dry. The crossing is short enough that a windy-morning postponement costs nothing; swap it with any Forio beach day.
spots.saveHtml: Save Procida is a half-day done cheaply: ferry, one climb to Terra Murata, granita, ferry home.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A long harbor-front lunch at Corricella facing the pastel amphitheater — the single most photographed table setting in the Bay of Naples.
spots.restoHtml:
• Corricella harbor front — fried fish cones, pasta and pizza at the water’s edge
  • Via Roma near the port — gelato and granita for the walk back
  • Ferry-day picnic — Forio bakeries pack focaccia for the crossing
spots.altboxHtml:
• Pompeii instead? Honest answer: from Ischia it burns 3–4 hours of ferry + train each way. It only fits this trip as a departure-day add-on with a late flight, or by adding a Naples overnight. Tickets are about $22 (Express) with a timed-entry cap — and note US-citizen kids pay; the EU under-18 free rule does not apply.
  • Capri is deliberately skipped — the family has already been; Procida is the new island.

days.heading: Giro dell’isola boat day
days.feel: Sea caves and swim stops by boat
days.note: The classic full-day boat circle of the island — sea caves, cliff villages from the water, and swim stops the buses can’t reach — runs about $80 per person with lunch. In the evening, Sorgeto’s free hot-spring cove is the volcanic party trick: thermal water bubbling straight into the sea.

days.heading: Sant’Angelo + Maronti
days.feel: The car-free south coast, then pack

facts.label: Flex
facts.valueHtml: This day absorbs any weather postponement

days.note: Sant’Angelo is the whitewashed, car-free village on the sand isthmus; Maronti is the island’s longest beach, with fumaroles steaming in the sand. This is also the week’s pressure valve — anything the wind cancelled lands here.

days.heading: Forio → Naples → Pittsburgh
days.feel: Boat, plane, home the same day

facts.label: Route
facts.valueHtml: Hydrofoil → NAP → EWR → PIT · same-day arrival

days.note: Take an early hydrofoil with real slack — Sunday-morning boats toward Naples are the ones that sell out, so book this leg ahead. United’s Naples departure lands you in Pittsburgh the same evening, four clear days before the Jun 24–26 commitment.

Where You Will Go

One island, one bay, no car

Everything moves by bus and boat. Forio anchors the west coast; the castle and the ferries sit on the east side, twenty minutes across.

PIT–NAP sells June 12–20 from about $1,353 per traveler with one stop, including Air Canada/United and British Airways options. The current family airfare band remains sound.

Getting to Ischia

One connection, then a boat

United’s Newark–Naples nonstop is the clean single-ticket play from Pittsburgh. Mid-June is its one-flight-a-day window, so the EWR connection deserves real slack.

Preferred outbound

DateSat Jun 12 · overnight
RoutePIT → EWR → NAP · United, single ticket
Family air band$4,400–$5,900 with bags/seats
BackupDelta JFK–NAP daily · ITA via FCO
United has ~6 PIT–EWR flights a day, so book the connection with hours of slack, not minutes. A misconnect in the 1x-daily window costs 24 hours.

The bay crossing

Airport → portAlibus · ~$6pp · every 15–30 min
HydrofoilAlilauro Beverello → Forio direct · ~50 min
Current faresAbout $26 adult · $18 child 2–12 · bags $4
Rough sea?Slow car ferry from Porta di Massa almost never cancels
Book the Sunday-morning return boat ahead — those are the sailings that sell out. Everything else can be bought the day before.

What Could Change

Wind, one flight a day, and a pool rule

The plan is bus-simple, but three specific things deserve watching. None of them is a reason to skip the trip; all three are reasons to build slack.

Act now

The EWR connection is the trip’s pinch point

Mid-June is United’s one-flight-a-day window to Naples. Book PIT–EWR with hours of slack, and know the Delta JFK–NAP daily exists as a same-day rescue.

Watch

Hydrofoils cancel in chop; car ferries don’t

Alilauro suspends around 2-meter waves. The mitigation is built in: the slow ferry from Porta di Massa keeps sailing, and the return morning has a spare boat’s worth of buffer.

Watch

Poseidon’s under-12 thermal rule

The 8-year-old gets the beach and three seawater pools, not the hot pools. Plan the split-parent rotation, or pick Negombo where the rule runs by height instead.

Good

June is Ischia’s driest, calmest month

About 79°F, seven brief rain days, and Festa della Repubblica crowds gone two weeks before arrival. Sea state problems are isolated storm events, not a pattern.

Juneteenth saves a PTO day

Saturday out, Sunday home, four PTO days, and back four clear days before the family’s Jun 24–26 Pittsburgh commitment.

Verdict: mid-June already clears the warm-water bar that defines this trip. Waiting a week buys a marginal sea-temperature gain and costs the Juneteenth PTO trick plus the pre-peak hotel pricing.

Keep it near the floor

  • Book United the day 2027 inventory loads — June is the route’s priciest month.
  • Half-board hotel deals cover the picky-eater dinners cheaply.
  • Poseidon’s afternoon ticket saves about $22; Sorgeto and San Montano are free.
  • Weekly bus passes, not taxis: about $65 covers the family’s whole week.

Worth paying for

  • The full-day giro dell’isola boat — the island’s best day, unreachable by bus.
  • A hotel whose thermal pools you’d actually use every evening.
  • The floodlit-castle dinner in Ischia Ponte.

Family Fit

Warm water carries everyone

This is the rare trip where the 8-year-old’s perfect day and the teenager’s perfect day are the same day, just in different pools.

For the 13-year-old

real range, real freedom

  • All 22 Poseidon pools, including the 104°F ones.
  • Cliff-jumping spots on the boat day and Sorgeto’s natural hot spring.
  • Procida’s photo game is genuinely strong.

For the 8-year-old

shallow, warm, sandy

  • San Montano and Maronti are shallow-entry, 74°F beaches.
  • The castle has an elevator, ramparts and a gelato terrace.
  • Boats replace car time — every transfer is part of the fun.

For picky eaters

the pizza homeland

  • Pizzeria Di Meglio and La Tinaia cover plain pizza and pasta in Forio.
  • Half-board hotel dining guarantees a known dinner.
  • Corricella’s harbor fries fish in paper cones — chicken-nugget adjacent.

Trip Balance

The most water-forward week on the board

Half of this trip happens in, on or beside warm water. Towns fill the evenings; the one hike is optional.

30%
